Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business coverage across major outlets is dominated by two intertwined stories: Trump's sweeping new tariffs on China and 13 other trading partners, and continued turbulence in AI-related stocks tied to the fallout from the Nvidia/Jensen Huang scandal. Secondary threads include the selection of Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next ECB president, tightening U.S. export controls on AI chips to Southeast Asia, and scattered retail and corporate M&A news.

stories.headline: Trump Unveils New Tariffs on China, EU and 12 Other Trading Partners
stories.summary: The administration proposed new Section 301 tariffs including a 20% rate on most Chinese imports that could rise to 40% if trade talks break down, alongside 15% levies on the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland, and up to 35% on Vietnam.

stories.headline: Wall Street Whipsaws as AI Trade Euphoria Turns to Gloom
stories.summary: The Nasdaq composite plunged as much as 4.5% before paring losses in a wildly volatile session, as the brief rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia quickly faded amid renewed doubts about AI spending sustainability.

stories.headline: Nvidia Halts Chip Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Export Rules
stories.summary: A new U.S. rule now requires licenses for companies in four Southeast Asian countries to buy advanced AI chips, part of a broader crackdown on Chinese access to computing power following the Jensen Huang scandal.

stories.headline: Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos Set to Become Next ECB President
stories.summary: The Spanish economist is set to succeed Christine Lagarde after the Dutch government withdrew support for rival candidate Klaas Knot, putting him in charge of the eurozone's fight against inflation.

stories.headline: S&P Puts Nvidia on 'CreditWatch Negative' Amid Governance Concerns
stories.summary: The credit rating agency warned it may cut Nvidia's AA rating over board independence and key-man risk tied to Jensen Huang, adding to a string of crises including chip export controls and credit-market jitters since his reinstatement as CEO.

stories.headline: Altria, Japan Tobacco Explore Breakup of Imperial Brands
stories.summary: Altria Group and Japan Tobacco are reportedly exploring a potential breakup of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands, which would rank among the largest takeovers in the sector.

stories.headline: Retail Earnings Point to Resilient Holiday Season, Led by Best Buy
stories.summary: Best Buy posted its strongest comparable sales growth in five years and raised full-year guidance, part of a broader pattern of retail turnarounds ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Business.gaps: Business Insider, Puck, Forbes, and The Information block direct web search for general queries, so coverage for those outlets relies on search snippets that surfaced; Politico's feed items were largely unrelated to business and politics-adjacent tariff coverage was not found.

US politics.overview: US politics coverage this period centers on President Trump's new wave of tariffs on China and other trading partners amid Democratic objections, a high-stakes Senate Democratic leadership battle between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen ahead of a Dec. 1 vote, and the House's push to pass a bipartisan energy permitting bill before the holiday recess. Courts remain active with rulings against the FCC's review of ABC licenses and against Trump's birthright citizenship order, while Cook Political Report and other outlets assess the scale of the GOP's midterm losses.

stories.headline: Trump administration proposes sweeping new tariffs on China, EU and other trading partners
stories.summary: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs targeting China (20%), the EU, and more than a dozen other economies over alleged industrial overcapacity, pressing ahead with its trade agenda despite a Democratic midterm sweep fueled by affordability concerns; China warned it could retaliate.

stories.headline: Schumer and Van Hollen battle for Senate Democratic leader ahead of Dec. 1 vote
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is mounting an underdog challenge to Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, framing himself as the change candidate who supports ending the filibuster and Medicare for All, with the secret-ballot vote set for Dec. 1.

stories.headline: House nears vote on bipartisan permitting reform bill
stories.summary: Speaker Mike Johnson is banking on Republican unity to pass the long-awaited Senate-passed permitting bill, with a rule vote expected Tuesday and final passage possibly Wednesday or Thursday, though its fate remains uncertain given GOP absences and limited Democratic support.

stories.headline: Federal judge blocks FCC's license review of ABC, calling it likely unconstitutional
stories.summary: A federal judge halted the FCC's review of ABC's broadcast licenses, finding it probably violates the First Amendment, after Disney and ABC argued the probe—nominally about diversity hiring—was political retribution by Trump-appointed FCC chair Brendan Carr.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report details scale of GOP midterm wreckage
stories.summary: Cook Political Report finds Republicans fell from 26 to just 20 governorships and from a 53-47 Senate majority to a 56-44 Democratic one, marking the party's worst Senate standing since 2008 as it assesses what can be salvaged after the midterms.

stories.headline: RNC leadership fight erupts as Republicans assign midterm blame
stories.summary: Trump's handpicked RNC chair is fighting off a challenge from a fellow Republican as the party wrestles internally over accountability for its midterm losses.

stories.headline: DC judge strikes down Trump's birthright citizenship restrictions again
stories.summary: Judge Christopher Cooper, whom Trump has publicly derided, struck down the administration's second attempt at restricting birthright citizenship, citing the Fourteenth Amendment and rejecting carve-outs based on surrogacy arrangements.

stories.headline: Lawmakers demand FBI, CIA briefings on Jensen Huang's Nvidia reinstatement
stories.summary: A Republican lawmaker is pushing for FBI and CIA briefings on what officials knew about potential national-security concerns before Jensen Huang's dramatic ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, with Schumer also vowing a Senate investigation.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no distinct recent political coverage found beyond stories already captured via other outlets; Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage reflected only what was visible in provided feed items or limited search snippets, since these outlets restrict broader search access.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's scandal-driven exit and swift reinstatement, with new developments on a possible credit downgrade and code-of-conduct fallout, alongside a parallel story of escalating US-China chip export controls squeezing both Nvidia's regional sales and Chinese AI labs. Several outlets are also tracking a volatile 'AI trade' on Wall Street, new AI safety and child-protection moves (Character.AI, AI toys, X parental controls), and the FCC's approval of SpaceX's plan for orbital AI data centers.

stories.headline: S&P weighs Nvidia credit downgrade and Jensen Huang's code-of-conduct breach reverberates internally
stories.summary: S&P is considering cutting Nvidia's credit rating to AA- over governance and 'key man' risks tied to Jensen Huang, even as reporting shows employees are unlikely to forget that Huang broke the company's own code of conduct; The Information separately reports S&P put Nvidia on 'CreditWatch Negative' and that Huang has apologized to staff and said he's in therapy.

stories.headline: Nvidia halts AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia as US tightens China-focused export controls
stories.summary: Nvidia stopped shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after a new US rule required licenses for advanced AI chip purchases in the region, part of a broader effort to close loopholes benefiting China.

stories.headline: Huawei becomes central to China's AI push as US chip curbs bite
stories.summary: As Nvidia's advanced chips become harder for Chinese firms to obtain, Huawei is emerging as an increasingly indispensable domestic alternative despite lagging US technology, and a separate report says Chinese labs like DeepSeek are already feeling the pressure from chip and anti-distillation restrictions.

stories.headline: FCC approves SpaceX plan for up to 1 million orbital AI data-center satellites
stories.summary: The FCC dismissed objections from opponents—including risks to scientific research—ruling they fell outside its authority, clearing SpaceX to eventually deploy a satellite constellation roughly 50 times the current number of objects in orbit for AI computing.

stories.headline: 42 state attorneys general move to block Character.AI from selling user chat data
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 state AGs filed near-identical objections seeking to stop Character.AI from selling off users' chat data as part of its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Dario Amodei pushes back on claims AI labs are ceding control to AI
stories.summary: Amodei called accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI 'absurd,' even as frontier labs increasingly automate their own research; a companion report has him separately calling the idea of AI governing society 'a bad idea.'

stories.headline: 1Password confirms hackers accessed internal systems and some customer data
stories.summary: The password manager said an attacker compromised an employee's corporate account and obtained some customer information, though it maintains that stored passwords themselves were not exposed; The Register adds that the intruder also got at source code and planted malicious code in backend services.

stories.headline: Wall Street's AI trade swings wildly amid Nvidia turmoil
stories.summary: The Nasdaq plunged as much as 4.5% before paring losses in a volatile session, as investors continue to reassess the AI trade following Nvidia's leadership chaos; The Economist warns Huang's reinstatement 'will not be the AI boom's last' bailout, while Bloomberg notes global stocks later rebounded as the AI trade staged a comeback.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind's own site/blog did not surface distinct recent announcements beyond what The Decoder reported on Gemini research agents; Platformer, which blocks search beyond its own feed, had no new posts since Nov 23 due to a Thanksgiving publishing break.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the fallout from COP31's collapse in Antalya, the US permitting-reform push and its implications for data centers, and a reassessment of the AI-driven power boom after Nvidia-related turbulence. Utility-sector coverage continues to focus on data center deals, affordability politics after the midterms, and oil prices amid Middle East tensions.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse amid fossil-fuel fight
stories.summary: Carbon Brief is running extensive post-mortems on COP31 after a coalition of nearly 90 nations, led by the EU, rejected the proposed "Antalya pact" over the absence of explicit fossil-fuel transition language, with Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar and Russia resisting such language. Heatmap separately reported that the longest-ever UN climate summit fell into disarray after the European-led coalition refused to sign a joint statement that omitted a fossil-fuel phase-out reference.

stories.headline: Permitting bill's data center provisions divide energy and climate advocates
stories.summary: Heatmap examined how the new permitting bill would make it easier for data centers to connect to the grid while raising their power costs, with Rhodium Group estimating the rules could double data centers' energy costs and raise project costs 10%. Latitude Media reported the Senate cleared the permitting reform package after a bitter split among environmental groups.

stories.headline: Utilities juggle data-center gold rush with affordability backlash
stories.summary: Utility Dive's Q3 earnings roundup found utility executives shifting from touting data-center pipelines toward emphasizing load diversity and affordability concerns following the midterm elections; separately, Vistra's CEO said the midterms brought clarity that data-center interconnection queues had been overstated by speculative developers. Other Utility Dive pieces covered FirstEnergy's newly approved $2.5B West Virginia gas plant (opposed by consumer advocates over ratepayer risk) and TVA's $1.7B data-center deal under a new large-load tariff.

stories.headline: Oil prices climb as Middle East tensions cloud supply outlook
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported oil rose in thin holiday trading as investors weighed whether renewed Middle East hostilities threaten a recovery in the region's crude exports. WSJ similarly noted oil futures settled higher for a second straight session as Middle East tensions countered expectations of a looming global supply surplus.

stories.headline: AI power boom hits a reality check as Nvidia drama rattles energy stocks
stories.summary: WSJ argued the sharp correction in power stocks tied to the AI buildout is creating investment opportunities, while Latitude Media reported energy and startup firms were "whiplashed" by Nvidia-related turmoil as CEO Jensen Huang's personal role in deals earned him the nickname "the bank of Huang." FT separately reported Nvidia halted chip shipments to Southeast Asia as the US tightened export controls to block Chinese access to AI computing power.

stories.headline: Michigan moves to rein in utilities and pause data-center growth
stories.summary: Latitude Media reported that Michigan Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson and Democratic lawmakers are preparing rules to tie utility profits to reliability performance and pause new data-center construction.

stories.headline: Midterm wins push Democrats toward a more moderate energy message
stories.summary: Heatmap reported that newly elected Democrats, including Senator-elect Annie Andrews of South Carolina, campaigned on cutting fossil-fuel taxes and an "all of the above" energy approach while still backing restoration of solar and wind tax credits, signaling a shift in Democratic climate politics after big election wins.

Energy.gaps: Could not find outlet-verified recent coverage from Argus Media; NYT and The Economist (search-blocked) had no relevant feed items provided.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by a fast-moving Chinese Communist Party shake-up after Shanghai's Politburo-ranked party chief Chen Jining was placed under investigation, and by a fresh round of US tariff and export-control moves targeting China and Southeast Asia. Business titles are tracking Chinese EV/auto expansion deals (BYD-Ineos), corporate settlements (SHEIN) and signs of a cooling domestic economy even as global investors warm to Chinese equities.

stories.headline: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining placed under investigation
stories.summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Shanghai's Communist Party Secretary Chen Jining has been placed under investigation, becoming one of the most high-profile officials caught up in Xi Jinping's anti-corruption drive just months before a major leadership reshuffle; Caixin notes he is the fourth sitting Politburo member probed since 2022, part of a tally of 61 senior officials investigated in 2026.

stories.headline: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on China and 13 other economies
stories.summary: State-run Xinhua reports that China's Commerce Ministry "firmly opposes" new Section 301 tariffs the US Trade Representative proposed on 14 economies over alleged "overcapacity," calling it unilateralism that violates WTO rules, while urging Washington to implement an already-agreed $30 billion reciprocal tariff-cut arrangement; state-run Global Times separately warned the move "risks offsetting trade negotiation gains, business confidence."

stories.headline: Nvidia halts advanced AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia
stories.summary: The New York Times reports Nvidia halted chip sales to four Southeast Asian countries after a new US rule requiring licenses for companies there to buy advanced AI chips, part of tightened efforts to block Chinese access; Caixin similarly flagged that new restrictions on advanced chips and remote computing access are raising uncertainty for Chinese tech firms' cloud contracts and investments.

stories.headline: BYD in exclusive talks to buy Ineos's French factory
stories.summary: CnEVPost and Caixin report that BYD has entered exclusive negotiations to acquire Ineos Automotive's Hambach, France plant, which Caixin notes would give the Chinese automaker its first passenger-car plant in Western Europe as trade barriers push it to localize production.

stories.headline: SHEIN to pay $100 million to settle US FTC allegations
stories.summary: TechNode reports SHEIN agreed to a $100 million consumer-redress settlement over FTC allegations involving shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews and misleading supply-chain claims; Caixin adds that the FTC claims the fast-fashion giant "harmed consumers by breaking its shipping promises and suppressing negative reviews," which the platform denies.

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty in US criminal trial
stories.summary: Taipei Times flags that Huawei was found guilty in a US case; Caixin reports the company and three subsidiaries were convicted on 10 counts but acquitted of racketeering charges, with sentencing scheduled for September 2027.

stories.headline: Economists urge Beijing to roll out more stimulus as demand weakens
stories.summary: Caixin reports that Chinese economists called for additional stimulus after October data showed weakening domestic demand, with a Renmin University economist proposing a 3 trillion yuan ($450 billion) fiscal package financed through added bond issuance, even as another economist said China faces little pressure to hit its 2026 growth target.

stories.headline: Hong Kong marks first anniversary of deadly Tai Po/Wang Fuk Court fire
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press ran extensive anniversary coverage of the blaze that killed 168 people, including survivor accounts, memorial masses and public mourning a year on, alongside a piece questioning whether the government's regulatory response has been adequate.

China.gaps: Could not find distinct recent coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, CGTN, Yicai Global, China Daily, Focus Taiwan or ChinaTalk via search; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ and The Economist are reported only via the feed items provided since they block search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the widening regional conflict: a deadly Iranian drone strike on Kuwait, repeated Houthi strikes on Riyadh's financial district, and fallout from the broader Iran war on oil markets and Tehran's economy. Alongside the security crisis, outlets are tracking an escalating Baghdad-Erbil oil dispute, Israeli coalition maneuvering, and Gulf sovereign wealth diplomacy ahead of a G20 investment summit.

stories.headline: Two Italians killed in Iranian drone attack in Kuwait
stories.summary: Kuwait's Defence Ministry said two people, including Italian nationals, were killed by shrapnel from intercepted Iranian drones targeting a vital site in the country.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Riyadh's tallest tower for second time in a week
stories.summary: Arab states and the Muslim World League condemned a Houthi drone attack on the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's financial district that injured 11 civilians, the second strike on the building in less than a week.

stories.headline: Baghdad-Erbil oil feud deepens as Iraq moves to seize Kurdish border crossings
stories.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister al-Zaidi's move to assert federal control over Kurdish border crossings and oilfields has sharpened tensions with Erbil, with Asharq Al-Awsat reporting a national dialogue effort now underway to defuse the crisis over federalism.

stories.headline: Iran's economy strains under 'silent war' of US blockade
stories.summary: WSJ reports that cuts to Iranian subsidies for fuel and food are putting new pressure on the public and exposing internal political divisions as the US blockade persists.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise as investors weigh Middle East supply risks
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports oil rose in thin holiday trading as markets assessed whether renewed Gulf hostilities threaten a recovery in the region's crude exports, after The National noted Brent rebounding toward $95 following a Saudi refinery drone attack.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed minister
stories.summary: Medics said Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight in Gaza, including a Hamas-appointed deputy education minister.

stories.headline: Likud officials expect Eisenkot to form government without Netanyahu's party
stories.summary: Sources close to Israeli coalition talks say roughly three-quarters of the details for a new government led by Eisenkot have been finalized, with Likud sidelined and haredi parties expressing confidence in the emerging deal.

stories.headline: Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute chairman seeks to bring $60tn in capital to G20 summit
stories.summary: The Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute's chairman is pushing to mobilize a combined $60 trillion in assets from global sovereign funds for the upcoming G20 investment summit in Miami.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find recent relevant coverage from Khaleej Times, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Times of Israel, Ynetnews, Iran International, Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist, or BBC in the material available.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this week spans West and Central African security flashpoints (DRC-Uganda diplomatic tensions, Nigeria's herder-farmer violence), major economic policy moves (Nigeria's dollar intervention, Congo's cobalt export ban) and a deadly infrastructure disaster in Egypt. Business and tech outlets are also tracking shifting investment flows between Nigeria and Kenya and continued turbulence in Francophone Africa's budget politics.

stories.headline: DRC-Uganda tensions escalate as Kinshasa summons Ugandan diplomat
stories.summary: Kinshasa has summoned a Ugandan diplomat after inflammatory comments from Uganda's army chief, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, deepened friction between the two neighbors already strained by the eastern Congo conflict.

stories.headline: Nigeria boosts retail dollar supply to curb naira volatility
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has approved a sharp increase in dollar sales to retail customers in an effort to boost liquidity and stabilize the naira.

stories.headline: Congo to reimpose cobalt export ban as prices slide
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo, the world's top cobalt producer, is set to reinstate a ban on exports of the battery metal by the end of the month in a bid to arrest a slump in prices, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Death toll rises to 31 after fuel truck inferno on Cairo highway
stories.summary: At least 31 people have died after an overturned fuel truck triggered a massive blaze that engulfed nearby vehicles on a Cairo highway, with emergency crews still responding.

stories.headline: UN rights chief warns of escalation risk in western Nigeria violence
stories.summary: The UN human rights chief has warned that attacks and reprisals tied to herder-farmer disputes in western Nigeria, which have already killed dozens, risk spiraling further.

stories.headline: Senegal's parliament denounces president over budget decree
stories.summary: Senegal's parliament adopted a resolution criticizing President Bassirou Diomaye Faye for implementing a 2026 budget bill that lawmakers had previously rejected, deepening a standoff that outlets have linked to risks for the country's IMF rescue program.

stories.headline: Haftar meets Erdogan as Turkey courts rival sides in Libya
stories.summary: Libyan commander Khalifa Haftar met Turkish President Erdogan as Ankara tries to position itself as a unifying broker between Libya's rival factions while protecting its own Eastern Mediterranean gas claims.

stories.headline: Why Nigerian companies are choosing Kenya for their next move
stories.summary: Nigerian firms including Dangote and Moniepoint are expanding into Kenya across energy, banking and capital markets, reflecting a broader shift in cross-border African corporate investment.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no verifiable coverage from the last 48 hours (most retrievable editions were months old). Africa Confidential's most recent retrievable stories (Museveni succession, Senegal IMF rescue, Tanzania sanctions) were over a week old and fell outside the recency window. FT, NYT, WSJ and AP block search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so they could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-industry outlets are dominated by a major press-freedom ruling against the FCC in its fight with ABC/Disney, plus continuing fallout from Skydance's CNN-CBS News cost-cutting as the two newsrooms prepare to merge. Secondary threads include a new UK probe into BBC antisemitism claims, Huw Edwards breaking his silence on camera, and publishers pushing back against AI bots and assistants like Meta's Muse.

stories.headline: Judge Blocks FCC's Early License Renewal Push Against ABC, Calling Case Retaliatory
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan handed ABC and Disney a major First Amendment victory, ruling the FCC's early license-renewal order was likely retaliation for the network's coverage of Trump and Jimmy Kimmel, and halting the process with an injunction.

stories.headline: Skydance's Cost-Cutting Tears Through CNN and CBS News Ahead of Planned Merger
stories.summary: More than a thousand CNN and CBS News staffers were offered voluntary buyouts as part of a roughly $6 billion cost-cutting push under new owners David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, fueling staff anger and uncertainty about the two newsrooms' eventual integration.

stories.headline: Bob Woodward's Rebuke of Jeff Bezos Resonates Inside The Washington Post
stories.summary: Veteran reporter Bob Woodward's sharp criticism of Washington Post owner Jeff Bezos has struck a chord with Post staffers who privately share similar frustrations with the billionaire owner, according to Status.

stories.headline: BBC Faces Government Investigation Over Antisemitism Claims
stories.summary: The UK government's independent antisemitism adviser, Lord John Mann, has opened a probe into the BBC after a former producer described the broadcaster as a hostile environment for openly Jewish staff.

stories.headline: Huw Edwards Breaks Silence on Conviction in New Channel 4 Documentary
stories.summary: Disgraced former BBC anchor Huw Edwards will speak publicly for the first time about his conviction for making indecent images of children in an upcoming Channel 4 documentary.

stories.headline: Wall Street Journal Joins Publishers Blocking AI Bots by Default
stories.summary: Dow Jones has overhauled its approach to automated crawlers, becoming the latest major publisher to disallow bots by default as news organizations grow wary of AI scraping their content.

stories.headline: Publishers Urged to Fight Back Against Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots Assistants
stories.summary: Press Gazette argues that new AI personal assistants from Meta and OpenAI are siphoning value from journalism without compensating publishers, as separate data shows Meta's Muse already driving a huge surge in AI agent traffic to retail sites this Cyber Week.

stories.headline: Gérard Depardieu to Stand Trial on Rape Charges After Losing Appeal
stories.summary: A Paris court rejected Gérard Depardieu's appeal, sending the French actor to criminal trial on rape charges stemming from a 2018 accusation by actress Charlotte Arnould.

Media.gaps: WSJ, FT, The Guardian and NYT block search, so coverage for them is limited to the single feed item provided (WSJ's story on a detained Japanese reporter in Russia); no other recent items from those outlets were available.
